searchText: Is there a writeup anywhere of the benefits to Solidity and the app layer of EOF? I don't (yet) understand (but want to). > allow invalid EOF initcode in txs This means that the VM cannot assume that the initcode is valid when run, like it can for other EOF code. If we really, really don't want to validate initcode then it shouldn't be EOF code at all. it still validates the EOF, it just charges the user basically don't tie the _validity_ of a transaction to the _validity_ of initcode -- if the initcode is invalid, charge the user the intrinsic cost of the tx and update their nonce

excerpts.content:
> allow invalid EOF initcode in txs
This means that the VM cannot assume that the initcode is valid when run, like it can for other EOF code.  If we really, really don't want to validate initcode then it shouldn't be EOF code at all.
